title: CAR verify() does not regress to allowing a double-verify race (guard for fixed defect CD-003)
description: CD-003 ('CAR verify() race condition — read-check-update without atomic lock') was marked fixed by replacing the read-check-update pattern with a single conditional findOneAndUpdate (corrective-action.service.js:789-860). This regression case guards against a future refactor reintroducing a non-atomic read-then-write.
steps: Fire two concurrent verify() calls from two different, valid verifiers against the same CAR
expectedResult: Exactly one call succeeds and transitions the CAR to a terminal verification outcome; the losing call receives a conflict response rather than both succeeding and appending two verificationHistory entries with contradictory outcomes.

title: Closed audit cannot be reverted to draft via direct PATCH (guard for fixed defect H-001, pending re-verification)
description: H-001 ('No audit status state machine — closed -> draft possible via direct PATCH') was marked fixed by routing status changes through changeStatus() (audit-assurance.controller.js:608). However, AUDIT_TRANSITIONS itself (audit.model.js:253-259) has a separate, since-discovered enum mismatch (see AUDT-UNIT-007: 'active' vs 'in_progress', missing 'archived') — this case re-verifies the original H-001 fix still holds independent of that separate issue.
expectedResult: The request is rejected because changeStatus()'s AUDIT_TRANSITIONS map has no outgoing edges from 'closed' (closed: []). The audit's status remains 'closed'. Note: if this test fails alongside AUDT-UNIT-007's finding on 'in_progress', re-verify whether changeStatus() is genuinely called on this code path or bypassed.

title: Duplicate field definitions in audit.model.js do not cause inconsistent persisted values for isoVersion/auditObjective/recurrence
description: Live defect M-005: isoVersion, auditObjective, and recurrence are each defined twice in audit.model.js (lines 122-140 and again at 193-214). Mongoose typically lets the later definition win, but this guard verifies persistence is actually consistent rather than silently dropping updates to whichever definition doesn't win.
steps: Create an audit and set isoVersion='2022', auditObjective='Test objective', recurrence='annual'
Reload the audit from the database and inspect these three fields
expectedResult: All three fields persist and read back exactly as set, with no field silently reverting to a default from the duplicate (losing) schema definition. Flag for remediation regardless of pass/fail: remove the duplicate field blocks in audit.model.js.

title: Marking a scope item 'not_applicable' still requires no justification and creates no SoA entry (guard that D-24 remains open)
description: Live defect D-24 (open): setting a scope item's status to 'not_applicable' requires no justification text and creates no corresponding Statement of Applicability entry, contrary to ISO 27001 Clause 6.1.3(c) which requires justification for exclusions.
preconditions: A scope item exists with status='in_progress'
steps: Set the scope item's status to 'not_applicable' with no justification text entered
Check the project's Statement of Applicability for a corresponding entry
expectedResult: Current behavior: the status change is accepted with no justification required, and no SoA entry is created or updated. This test intentionally documents D-24 is still open; re-classify to 'fixed' outcome once justification is enforced and an SoA entry is generated.
